name: Bash (incl. Git Bash on Windows)
summary: GNU Bash with GNU Readline. Ships with Git for Windows (Git Bash), every Linux distro, and as an old 3.2 on macOS.
startupCostMs: Measured on Windows 11 with Git for Windows 2.54 (median of 5): usr\bin\bash.exe --norc -i -c exit = 20 ms; bin\bash.exe --norc --noprofile = 35 ms; bin\bash.exe -l -i with stock /etc/profile = 258 ms; usr\bin\bash.exe -i with a modular rc = 158 ms. Each extra process (subshell, $(...), external tool) at startup costs 10-60 ms on Windows, ~1-5 ms on Linux. ble.sh on Windows costs 24-60 ms per keystroke and ~0.9 s per new tab.

install.notes: Git for Windows provides Git Bash (bash 5.x, MSYS2 runtime) at C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\bash.exe

windows.notes: Git Bash is MSYS2-based: ~ is %USERPROFILE%. Start usr\bin\bash.exe -i directly (not git-bash.exe or bin\bash.exe) to skip Git's launcher and /etc/profile; the profile must then rebuild PATH/MSYSTEM itself.

install.notes: macOS ships bash 3.2 (GPLv2) at /bin/bash: no PROMPT_COMMAND array, no EPOCHREALTIME, no globstar. Install 5.x with brew.

macos.notes: Terminal.app and iTerm2 start login shells, so ~/.bash_profile is read and ~/.bashrc is not unless it is sourced from there. The default login shell is zsh since macOS 10.15.

linux.notes: Terminal emulators usually start non-login interactive shells (read ~/.bashrc); display managers and ssh start login shells (read ~/.bash_profile, else ~/.profile).

prompt.notes: PS1 + PROMPT_COMMAND; no native transient or right prompt.

line-editing.notes: GNU Readline via ~/.inputrc; no built-in autosuggestions or syntax highlighting (ble.sh adds them, slow on Windows).

colors.notes: No syntax highlighting in plain readline; LS_COLORS drives ls and completion colors.
